post.caption: Fans helped buy back Jane Austen's ring. It is a small gold ring set with a blue turquoise, one of only three surviving pieces of jewelry known to have belonged to her, and it stayed in her family for nearly 200 years. Sotheby's sold it in London in July 2012 for more than five times its high estimate, and its stone was first thought to be a fossil tooth. Singer Kelly Clarkson later said she was the winning bidder. Britain paused the export, fans around the world donated, and Clarkson accepted the museum's offer in September 2013. The ring went on display at Jane Austen's House on Valentine's Day, 2014.
